title: Inference pathway autotuner: consolidate prefill/decoder scheduling with arch/length-aware kernel routing
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce tail latency and token cost across mixed workloads by centralizing the decision logic that chooses execution code paths (kernels) and prefill/decode scheduling strategies.

Scope: Design and implement an "inference pathway" layer that: (1) consolidates per-request signals (model variant, GPU architecture, sequence length bucket, attention sparsity heuristic, KV cache hit/miss history) into a compact fingerprint; (2) maps fingerprints to an execution plan that includes kernel selection, attention tile strategy, and whether to prefer aggressive batching or low-latency prefill choices; (3) exposes an online autotuner that adjusts routing policies using low-overhead probes and a bandit-like update rule.

Approach summary:
- Offline profiling: run microbenchmarks across representative seq-len distributions and hardware (A100, H100, L4/4x) to build a kernel performance table keyed by (arch, model-size, seqlen, decode-vs-prefill).
- Fingerprint & bucketing: avoid per-request heavy hashing by using a two-stage key: coarse bucket by seqlen quantiles and arch, plus a compact attention-profile id for long-form vs chat-style patterns.
- Hybrid routing policy: start with an offline-recommended kernel for each bucket, allow the online tuner to incrementally try alternative kernels during low-risk traffic to validate improvements. Use Thompson-sampling-inspired updates to prefer lower-latency/lower-cost choices while respecting p99 safety budgets.
- Prefill/Decode coupling: treat prefill scheduling (how many tokens to prefetch and whether to prioritize KV cache reuse) as part of the plan; e.g., for long-prefill workloads prefer memory-friendly attention tiling kernels, for short chat bursts prefer single-step low-latency kernels.
- Probing: use micro-probes (1-5% of requests) with synthetic sequence slices to estimate delta to baseline and to detect regression. Probes are rate-limited and tagged to avoid billing or access issues.
- Telemetry: augment existing request traces with pathway decisions and probe outcomes. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU-util, kernel-change failure rate, KBs of KV cache saved.

Success metrics and targets:
- Tail latency: reduce p95 latency by 10-20% for mixed seqlen workloads on Dedicated pools.
- Cost: reduce tokens-per-second equivalent cost by 12-18% for throughput sensitive workload mix.
- Stability: kernel-change rollback rate < 0.5% during canary.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated benchmark harness and dashboard demonstrating win on three standard workloads (chat, long-document, code completion).
- Canary rollout path with automatic rollback on p99 regressions.
- Integration tests for prefill/decoder coupling and telemetry tags.
- Documentation: design doc and operator runbook for tuning knobs.
comments: 2026-02-11: Initial spike completed — offline profiling scripts (profiling/arch_matrix_v2) produced a candidate kernel performance table. Observed strong variation for seqlen>1024 on H100 when using attention tiling vs fused kernels.

2026-02-18: Design review with runtime and infra teams. Feedback: avoid per-request heavy hashing, ensure probes are rate-limited, and make canary threshold configurable. Action: update design to use two-stage fingerprinting and explicit probe budget per pool.

2026-02-25: Prototype: implemented pathway router shim in the serving runtime that selects kernel id from a config map. Microbench results show 14% p95 improvement on mixed chat/long-doc synthetic workload with conservative policy. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234

2026-03-03: PR review notes from Alice Nguyen: need stronger isolation between probe instrumentation and billing, and a deterministic seed for bandit exploration to aid reproducing regressions. Added tasks to address both.

2026-03-08: Integration test flake found where KV cache reuse metadata wasn't propagated when routing switched kernels; root cause: older encoder didn't emit 'kv_schema_v2' tag. Patch in flight: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1278

2026-03-12: Re-ran benchmarks after kv_schema patch; p95 wins persist, but observed a 0.7% increase in GPU memory pressure on certain kernels. Deciding mitigation: add memory-safety check to runtime and fallback to conservative kernel when memory headroom < 200MB.
Open questions: define safe probe budget for Dedicated customers; policy for customer-configured conservative-only mode; telemetry retention window needed for reliable bandit updates.
